content.comment_body: You need to clarify your requirements more specifically if you want helpful answers. What exactly are you trying to accomplish with the VFD? Please provide more details, as general questions tend to result in broad responses.

Hello [user_name], I want to use [product_name] to send start, stop, and speed commands and monitor alarms via Modbus TCP. My intention is to control these functions through Modbus TCP communication, similar to how [version_no] communicates with a VFD. I'm working with an Opti drive E3 VFD and aiming for similar control.
Hi, I am interested to know if [product_name] is capable of reading and writing data with a VFD.

Modbus RTU isn't supported on [product_name]; only Modbus TCP/IP is possible. You may need a gateway that converts Modbus RTU to Modbus TCP/IP, though finding a reliable gateway is crucial to avoid connection issues. Cheaper solutions might not work well. Sometimes, you can get a Modbus TCP/IP expansion card for your VFD, which could also be an option. Regards, [user_name]

If your [product_name] controller supports Modbus, it's limited to Modbus TCP/IP, not Modbus RTU. A gateway might be needed to bridge Modbus TCP/IP to Modbus RTU, but I can't confirm details since I haven't done this myself.
Hello all, Could you provide details on how [product_name] communicates via TCP/IP with field devices like VFDs, specifically how to read and write data from them?
You have asked this same question elsewhere: [url]

Regardless of the topic, it's important that you first provide detailed information about the inverter you are using, such as links to specifications and the related Modbus protocol documentation. Also clarify the specific controls you need from [product_name]. Regards, [user_name]

Hello, I use [product_name] to read data from an electricity meter. I utilize a Moxa MB3180 to convert Modbus RTU to Modbus TCP, and it's worked well for me. The conversion is straightforward, and configuring the Moxa 3180 only took about five minutes.

Hi [user_name], Here's a suggestion if you're considering a gateway. I located a brief guide for the Optidrive E3 online, though I'm not sure if it matches your VFD since you didn't provide specifics. I was able to set up a data exchange following those instructions.
Hello [user_name], Thank you very much for your suggestion. As you indicated, it looks like an RTU to TCP/IP gateway is necessary, correct?

This has already been mentioned previously. [product_name] (such as FS4 models) supports only Modbus TCP/IP. According to the manual, the VFD supports only Modbus RTU. Your topic title references RTU, not TCP/IP. You will likely need a gateway, since Modbus TCP/IP (Ethernet) and Modbus RTU (RS485) use different physical protocols.

Can you assist me? I have an identical drive and would like to complete a project using Modbus TCP. I'm not certain if the example provided refers to RTU. Can you let me know where I can find more information?
Could you help me? I have a drive similar to yours that I want to connect using Modbus TCP. According to the manual, the port operates as RTU.

Hello [user_name], Welcome! Please note this is an English-language forum, so kindly write future posts in English. Thank you. Could you assist me? I have the same drive and I'd like to communicate using Modbus TCP, but according to the product manual the port is RTU.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing how to connect [product_name] controllers to VFDs, with the main issue being Modbus RTU versus Modbus TCP/IP protocol compatibility. The main goal is to control and monitor VFDs using [product_name] via Modbus, but direct support is limited to Modbus TCP/IP. Solutions involving protocol-converting gateways are suggested, but add complexity and potential reliability concerns. Several users request example configurations and clear documentation for integrating field devices over Modbus TCP/IP.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] controllers to enable both reading from and writing to VFDs via Modbus, ideally supporting both RTU and TCP/IP protocols for comprehensive control and monitoring. Additionally, users are looking for practical step-by-step guidance on how to set up and configure this communication.
